summary: Describes sixteen new TLS cipher suites using elliptic curve cryptography that specify stronger message authentication than the HMAC-SHA-1 used earlier. Eight use HMAC with SHA-256 or SHA-384, and eight use AES in Galois Counter Mode. They give TLS 1.2 users stronger options for elliptic-curve key exchange.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds sixteen cipher suite choices for TLS connections that use elliptic-curve cryptography. The choices use SHA-256 or SHA-384 with AES-CBC, or use AES-GCM.

subtitle: Sixteen TLS cipher suites combine elliptic-curve key exchange with SHA-256, SHA-384 or AES-GCM.

tldr.problem: The elliptic-curve TLS suites in RFC 4492 used HMAC-SHA-1, while the IETF was moving toward stronger hash algorithms.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines sixteen suites: eight use AES-CBC with HMAC-SHA-256 or SHA-384, and eight use AES-GCM.
tldr.outcome: The new suites use elliptic-curve key exchange and signatures; the GCM suites require TLS 1.2 or greater. RFC 10015 later updates this RFC.

today: RFC 5289 is listed as a Proposed Standard in the batch metadata and is updated by RFC 10015.

sections.title: Why Add These Cipher Suites
sections.content:
RFC 4492 defined elliptic-curve cipher suites for Transport Layer Security (TLS), and those suites used HMAC-SHA-1 for message authentication. This RFC adds suites that use SHA-256 or SHA-384 instead.

TLS 1.2 also supports authenticated encryption modes. This document defines elliptic-curve suites using AES in Galois Counter Mode (GCM) as well as suites that use an HMAC-based message authentication code.
sections.plainLanguage: The existing elliptic-curve suites all used SHA-1 for message authentication. This RFC adds options using SHA-256, SHA-384 or GCM-based authenticated encryption.

sections.title: Two Families of Suites
sections.content:
The RFC defines sixteen cipher suites. All use elliptic-curve cryptography for key exchange and digital signatures, as specified in RFC 4492. The new suites change the message protection and hash choices.

Eight suites use AES in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with HMAC. Eight use AES in GCM mode. Suite names identify the key exchange, signature or certificate type, AES key size and hash function.
sections.plainLanguage: There are two groups of eight suites. One group uses AES-CBC with HMAC; the other uses AES-GCM.

sections.title: CBC Suites with HMAC
sections.content:
The first eight suites use AES in CBC mode and an HMAC message authentication code. For suites ending in _SHA256, both the TLS pseudorandom function (PRF) and HMAC use SHA-256. For suites ending in _SHA384, both use SHA-384.

These suites correspond to suites from RFC 4492, with the MAC and PRF algorithms changed. Their key-exchange and signature algorithms stay the same.
sections.plainLanguage: These suites use AES-CBC and add HMAC with SHA-256 or SHA-384. The matching hash also determines the TLS pseudorandom function.

sections.title: GCM Suites
sections.content:
The second group uses AES in Galois Counter Mode with authenticated encryption and additional data. The available algorithms are AEAD_AES_128_GCM and AEAD_AES_256_GCM. They use GCM as described for TLS in RFC 5288.

Because the authenticated-encryption algorithm provides integrity protection, this RFC specifies the PRF hash for these suites: SHA-256 or SHA-384, according to the suite name.
sections.plainLanguage: GCM combines encryption and authentication in one mode. The suite name still selects SHA-256 or SHA-384 for the TLS pseudorandom function.

sections.title: Use Limits and Assigned Values
sections.content:
The security considerations in RFC 4346, RFC 4492 and RFC 5288 also apply to these suites. As stated in RFC 5288, the suites in this document may be used only with TLS 1.2 or greater.

IANA assigned two-byte cipher suite values. The HMAC-based suites use values from 0xC0,0x23 through 0xC0,0x2A; the GCM-based suites use values from 0xC0,0x2B through 0xC0,0x32.
sections.plainLanguage: These suites require TLS 1.2 or later. Each suite has an assigned value so the peers can identify which one they select.
